text:
sylvie: Quick follow-up from the Dedicated pool RFC: we're moving to split admit/allocate calls. Drafting a short migration plan, need quick feedback.
noor: ok, what breaks for integrators?
sylvie: main change: admit returns an opaque admission token instead of a blocking lease. allocate(token) is the second call to observe allocation. We'll ship an operator shim to accept old single-call requests for a grace period.
dave: token design? avoid DB lookups ideally.
sylvie: propose HMAC'ed compact token: version|expiry|nonce|kid|sig (base64url). stateless verify with operator key; support key rotation by including kid.
felix: TTL suggestion: default 60s, configurable per-tenant. Add optional param block_until_allocated=true for clients that need old behavior while in shim mode.
noor: contract tests needed: v1 legacy flow, v2 admit-only -> allocate success, v2 admit->allocate timeout. Add a delayed-provision variant.
dave: observability: new spans operator.admit.v2 and operator.allocate.v2; metrics operator.api.v2_admits, operator.api.v2_alloc_success, operator.token.sig_errors.
felix: rollout: 1) ship operator shim to staging; 2) enable control-plane v2 header for small canary (10%); 3) run contract + perf; 4) expand to 50% for 7d; 5) remove shim after 14d if stable.
noor: rollback gates? define token.sig_mismatch > 0.5% or admit->allocate P95 regression > 30% as triggers. Also require ability to flip control-plane flag quickly.
sylvie: good. I'll write the runbook, include SDK helpers Orch.admit(..., block=false) and Orch.allocate(token), and tag devex for examples. tagging @deploy-bot for reminders.
deploy-bot: Reminder set: run admit/allocate canary checklist in 4 days (staging) and 11 days (prod canary).
